tagline.text: The heart of Southern Leyte, a port city with a cathedral and cave shrines

location.label: Location
location.text: Maasin City, Southern Leyte (southwestern Leyte Island)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500–3,500 (per person, 1 night 2 days, including transport, lodging, meals and fees)

children.text: Maasin City is the capital of Southern Leyte and the southwestern gateway port of Leyte Island, with boat connections to Cebu and Bohol. The site of an 18th-century Jesuit church, the cathedral, a shrine inside a cave, and Camp Danao with its waterfalls and zoo are all in one city, making it a handy base for Southern Leyte.
Maasin is the capital of Southern Leyte, at the southwestern end of Leyte Island. It covers about
212 km²

with 70 barangays, and the 2024 census counted 85,486 residents. People are called Maasinhon and mainly speak Cebuano, with the Boholano dialect and Tagalog also spoken. It is a third-class city with many Roman Catholics, and the cathedral is its center. To the west, across the Canigao Channel, lies Bohol.

The name is said to come from a story in which locals answered Spanish settlers looking for water with "maasin" (salty). The Jesuits set up the parish in the 1700s, and ruins of the first Jesuit church remain between Abgao and Mantahan. About 1 km away, a second church built under Augustinian oversight still stands. Japanese forces occupied the town on June 3, 1942, but local guerrillas, including Colonel Ruperto Kangleon, resisted. Maasin became the capital when Southern Leyte became a province in 1960 and a city on August 10, 2000. It was badly damaged by Typhoon Rai (Odette) in December 2021.

As a destination, Maasin is not a glamorous resort city but a small port city. In town you walk around the cathedral, the plaza and the market, and outside town you can enjoy cave shrines, waterfalls, beaches, Camp Danao with its zoo, and picnics on islands across the bay. One travel blogger described it as a quiet city showing that Southern Leyte, known mostly for typhoons and landslides, has more to see.

Maasin also serves as a transfer point for routes around southern Leyte and for trips from Bohol and Cebu. A typical plan takes in the church and plaza in town and the cave shrines and waterfalls outside the city in a day or two, then continues to Limasawa Island or Sogod Bay. Boat timetables, fares and opening hours change often, so please check with the city tourism office or operators before you go. August 10 (Charter Day) marks the city's founding with events, and Maasin is also known as a no-smoking city of Eastern Visayas. There are large stores such as Gaisano Grand Mall and Metro Gaisano, so shopping is easy.

blocks.title: Maasin Cathedral and the Jesuit church ruins

children.text: Maasin Cathedral is the seat of the Diocese of Maasin, founded on August 14, 1968, and is also the Our Lady of the Assumption parish church. It is within walking distance in town, and the public plaza across the street has a monument to José Rizal erected in 1930. The bishop's residence stands beside the cathedral. Please be quiet during Mass. You can also see the ruins of the first Jesuit church between Abgao and Mantahan and the older church about 1 km away.
This shrine of the Most Precious Blood is in Sitio Basak, Rizal, with a chapel built inside a hilltop cave and a statue of Our Lady of the Assumption about 9 m (30 ft) tall. It is about
2 km
from town and has a large-scale Way of the Cross. There are many steps, so wear comfortable shoes.

This natural park of about 320 hectares in Malapoc Sur has a lagoon, a cave, trails, a 360-degree viewing deck and a camp area, and is also used as a Boy Scouts of the Philippines jamboree site. The Maasin Zoo inside is described as having lions, tigers, tarsiers, camels and the Philippine eagle. It takes about
30 minutes
by car from town.
About
15 km

from the city center, with a large cave with stalactites and stalagmites, waterfalls and a natural swimming pool. Wikivoyage also lists Guinsohotan Falls and Busay Falls. The cave is dark, so you need a local guide and a headlamp.

blocks.title: Hapitan Beach and Mangrove Eco-Forest Park

children.text: A beach in Manhilo where sea water and fresh water mix. It is popular in summer and about 10–15 minutes from town by car. You can reach it by car or motorcycle.

blocks.title: Santo Niño Shrine and Pagatpat Islet

children.text: On Pagatpat Islet off Mahayahay, a shrine honors the barangay's patron saint. From the national highway it is about
10 minutes
on foot to the Pangpang area, then
3 minutes
by pump boat across.

blocks.title: Abiera's Museum and the Oppus house

children.text: Abiera's Museum displays ancient artifacts and personal collections, including items said to be linked to Magellan's men. The Oppus Ancestral House is listed as one of the city's old houses. Check opening hours locally.

blocks.title: Canigao Island and Banahaw Cold Spring

children.text: Canigao Island off Maasin appears in travel accounts as a place for camping and picnics. Banahaw Cold Spring in San Joaquin, Macrohon, is about
13 km
from Maasin,
20–30 minutes
by car.
Arrive in Maasin, drop your bags at your lodging, and walk around the cathedral, plaza and market.
Eat seafood at a restaurant near the market.
Take a tricycle up to Monte Cueva Shrine for a view over town, then look for the Jesuit church ruins.
Hire a vehicle to Guinsohotan Cave and the falls, or visit Camp Danao and the zoo.
Relax at Hapitan Beach or Banahaw Cold Spring, then move on according to your boat or bus time.
Falls and caves are slippery after rain, so leave slack in your schedule.

items.title: Transit route
items.subtitle: Half a day, arriving by boat from Cebu

children.text: Arrive at Maasin port on the boat from Cebu and look around the cathedral and plaza.
Visit Monte Cueva Shrine and have lunch.
Buy snacks at the market and take the boat or bus back.
Fly from Manila (NAIA) to Daniel Z. Romualdez Airport, Tacloban (TAC).
From Tacloban to Maasin, a van takes about
4 hours
(3.5–4 hours depending on the listing). A September 2026 booking guide lists Duptours vans several times a day at
(₱220 in a 2011 report), and fuel surcharges may push it higher. Some sources put the road trip at about 5 hours.
Maasin has an airstrip for general aviation, but scheduled service was reportedly suspended because of low demand.
Fast ferries (Weesam Express, OceanJet) to Cebu run from Maasin National Port and take about
3 hours
, departing at

(Weesam Express from Maasin, Mondays and Fridays, fares ₱750–900, per a September 2026 booking guide). The same guide lists OceanJet daily from Maasin at 15:30 (fares listed inconsistently at about ₱1,100–2,100) and a weekly Cokaliong RoRo sailing (about 5.5–6.5 hours, from ₱540). These are booking-site listings and fuel surcharges may raise fares, so confirm the latest schedule with the operator.
Another way is to take a jeepney to Bato port and board a ferry to Cebu (about
, per Wikivoyage, based on 2016–2019 data that may be out of date).
There are also notes about Cokaliong ships connecting Macrohon and Maasin, and boats to Ubay, Bohol.
Philtranco, DLTB, Ultrabus and CUL are described as serving the Manila–Maasin route. It takes about
23 hours
(from Pasay or Quezon City).
There are also routes through central Leyte via Ormoc and Baybay. Check timetables before boarding.
The town center can be covered on foot, and tricycles and motorcycle taxis are described as costing about
for short rides. Confirm the fare before you get in.
For the falls, caves and zoo outside town, hire a vehicle or a habal-habal.

Maasin has a tropical rainforest climate with about 2,300 mm of rain a year and about 83% humidity. The driest month is April (about 72 mm) and the wettest is December (about 286 mm). The average temperature is about
, and November–February is cooler at 22–28℃.
The cathedral and town sights work in any season, but the falls and beaches are best in the relatively dry February–April. June to October brings heavy rain and rough seas that can stop boats.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: December is the wettest month of the year, so take care at falls and caves.
The most reliable time for falls, beaches and outdoor plans.
Boats are easily canceled, so leave slack in your schedule.

Small lodgings cluster in town. The Wikivoyage listings (2016–2019) include GV Hotel beside the port (43 rooms, fan or air-conditioned, from about ₱475), Ampil Pensionne (fan single ₱150, air-conditioned double ₱450), Southern Comfort Pensionne (₱500–700) and DW Pensione in Abgao (from ₱350). The prices are old, so confirm them by phone before booking. One travel guide site describes guesthouses in the ₱400–1,200 range and mid-range hotels at ₱1,200–2,500, and says there is almost no luxury lodging in town.

Guides say you can eat seafood in fishing villages and at the market, and Wikivoyage lists Alberto's Pizza on Espina Street (from ₱80). You can shop at Metro Gaisano next to the bus terminal (9 AM–8 PM) and Prince Supermarket, and Metrobank and PNB are said to have 24-hour ATMs. Bring plenty of cash before heading to outlying sights with poor access.
The cathedral and plaza are walkable, so staying in town is convenient.
For the falls, caves and zoo it is easier to hire a vehicle, so ask your lodging or the tourism office for a recommendation.
Boat timetables to Cebu change often, so check with the port or operator the day before.
Caves require a headlamp and a local guide.
Monte Cueva has many steps, so wear comfortable shoes and avoid the midday sun.
Many market stalls and small shops take cash only. Withdraw at a town ATM beforehand.
Camping on Canigao Island off Maasin appears in travel accounts, so if you plan to camp, confirm permission and boats locally first.
Town hospitals reportedly include the provincial hospital and Sacred Heart Hospital. Bring basic medicines, but use local hospitals in an emergency.
Southern Leyte is prone to landslides from typhoons and heavy rain. If heavy rain is forecast, cancel falls, caves and mountain plans and check the latest weather notices.
After rain, falls and caves swell suddenly and the paths are slippery.
Some town streets are dark at night, so do not walk alone late at night.
Boats are canceled in bad weather, so leave slack on your return day.
The cathedral and shrines are places of worship. Dress modestly and be quiet during Mass.
A bay on the east side of Southern Leyte, known for diving, with Sogod Bay Scuba Resort in Padre Burgos about 45 minutes by car from Maasin.

An island reached by public banca (around 8 AM, about 45 minutes–1 hour) from Padre Burgos port, about 30 minutes by road from Maasin, known as the site of the first Catholic Mass in the Philippines. Blog guides list an entrance fee of about ₱25–50 (2022 and 2025) and a boat fare of about ₱70–100 (2025). There is no official fee schedule, so confirm locally.
